verses.rationale: Preserve the mixed personal-and-clan descent.

verses.rationale: Keep honor distinct from a moral ranking and preserve the pain wordplay.

verses.after: Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez, saying, “I bore him in pain.”

verses.rationale: Retain the concrete land request and pain link without turning the prayer into a universal promise.
verses.before: Jabez called upon the God of Israel, saying, "If you would bless me and enlarge my territory, may your hand be with me, and keep me from harm, so that it might not bring me pain!" God granted what he requested.
verses.after: Jabez called on the God of Israel: “If only you would bless me and enlarge my territory! Let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm so that I am free from pain.” God granted what he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jabez called upon the God of Israel, saying, "If you would bless me and enlarge my territory, may your hand be with me, and keep me from harm, so that it might not bring me pain!" God granted what he requested.

verses.rationale: Keep the brother relationship and both generations.

verses.after: Chelub, Shuhah’s brother, fathered Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.

verses.rationale: Retain the unnamed female subject rather than silently rearranging the next verse.

verses.rationale: Keep both maternal notices in source order and note their difficult relationship.
